evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.55, BOTTOM row, the 'alpha' arrow drawn right-to-left: allylic (radical-site) alpha-cleavage of the rearranged 1,3-hexadiene radical cation expels a methyl radical (written 'CH3.' on the page) and leaves the resonance-stabilised pentadienyl cation. Book draws 0 arc(s) on this step (only the 'alpha'-labelled reaction arrow and the two products); moves <1,2,3> are curator-supplied hooks required for electron balance, none of them drawn. Encoded flow: radical site C6 -> forming pi C6=C5; one electron of the sigma C5-C4 -> that forming pi; the second electron of C5-C4 -> C4 (the departing CH3.). RESONANCE (convention C): the book draws the cation with the charge on the TERMINAL carbon that used to carry the methyl (CH2=CH-CH=CH-CH2+); the arrows as encoded produce the other resonance form, with the charge on the central carbon C1 (CH2=CH-CH(+)-CH=CH2), because the odd electron at C6 is consumed by the new C5=C6 pi bond while the positive charge stays where record IMS8-EQ8.55c left it. Both are the same delocalised pentadienyl cation C5H7+.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.55; no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. The generic alkene alpha-cleavage rules (IMS_4_12_1/2, IMS_4_15_1_1/1_2) that would cover an allylic C-CH3 cleavage write the ionised alkene as a SINGLE carbon carrying both charge and spin ('[C+.]'), keeping the C=C bond intact - a form RDKit cannot represent for carbon (it would need five bonds on a cation) and therefore not the localisation used here; they also belong to the known Ch. 4 geometry-bug family (the cleaved bond is not incident to the pi-forming atom). RDKit substructure test of IMS_4_30's LHS '[#6;v3;+0]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6;v3;+1]-[#6]=[#6]' against this precursor gives 0 matches. No MOD rule reproduces the 8.55 methyl-loss step.

observed_mz 67.0542 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C5H7+ (electron-mass corrected). The page prints NO m/z and NO abundance for this ion: the only percentages on the page ('80%', '25%', '<=5%') belong to C4H6+., and the 'C5H8+.' named in the text below the scheme is a different, even-electron-loss ion (m/z 68) from the methylcyclohexene/cycloheptene isomers. Hence detected=false, status 'inferred', no relative_intensity.
